transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I can’t get near a scaffold, a roof edge, or an upper platform without feeling like I’m about to go over. Even when the rails are there and I know it’s supposed to be safe, my head keeps telling me I’m going to fall.
Did this fear start after a specific traumatic accident or event, such as a fall?
Yes. It started after the stair tower accident, about thirteen months ago.
Do you experience unwanted, distressing memories or flashbacks of that stair tower accident when you aren't trying to think about it?
I’m not sure what you mean by flashbacks. I don’t really sit around thinking about it unless something brings it up.
Have you had any nightmares or distressing dreams about the accident since it happened?
No, I haven’t noticed any nightmares or dreams about it.
Do you go out of your way to avoid heights or working up high altogether?

Yeah. I’ve been handing the height inspections off to my foremen and moving meetings down to ground level when I can. If I absolutely have to go up, I keep somebody right beside me and get through it as fast as I can, scared the whole time.
